newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares head south as profit taking arrives.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares head south as profit taking arrives.

text.p: Belgian shares turned south on Thursday after setting out mixed as light profit taking took hold of the market.

Dealers said they were not surprised by the move, coming after the Bel-20 leading share index .BFX rose 2.4 pct on Wednesday and with the prospect of Friday's end of the two-week forward market account.
"The market is so unrealistic, weird, unpredictable," one trader said of Wednesday's sharp up-move. Profit taking was likely. "I'm not sure about today but definitely tomorrow."
By 0835 GMT the Bel-20 was down 0.87 pct at 2,578.84 points.
In an investor note dated July 23, brokerage Corluy & Co said the market was being driven at present by two emotions: angst and greed -- a situation which could not last forever.
It was therefore time to start looking again at defensive stocks, it said.
Few shares bucked Thursday's trend. Exceptions included non-ferrous metals maker Union Miniere, up 20 francs at 3,335 francs, and chemicals maker Solvay.
Solvay, which is due to release first half results next week and will split its share in September, was up 50 francs at 22,750 francs.
